First, notice that $\triangle{ABC}$ is an equilateral triangle. Consequently, all of the interior angles must be equal to $60^\circ\mathbin{:}$

\[ m\angle{A}=m\angle{B}=m\angle{ABC}=60^\circ \]

Also, since $\triangle{CDB}$ is an isosceles triangle, the base angles must have equal measure:

\[ m\angle{CBD}=m\angle{D} \]

Notice also that $\angle{ACB}$ and $\angle{DCB}$ are supplementary, therefore, we obtain \begin{align*} m\angle{ACB} + m\angle{DCB} &= 180^{\circ} \\[3pt] 60^{\circ} +m\angle{DCB} &= 180^{\circ} \\[3pt] m\angle{DCB}&= 120^{\circ} . \end{align*}

Finally, we calculate $m\angle {D}$ using the fact that the interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} m \angle {D} + m \angle {DCB} + m \angle {CBD} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] m \angle {D} + 120^\circ + m \angle {D} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 2m \angle {D}&= 60^\circ \\[3pt] m \angle {D} &= 30^\circ \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Measure of an Angle Given Multiple Triangles

question.text: In the isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$ with base $\overline{AB}$, point $E$ lies on the side $\overline{BC}$, $\overline{AE} = \overline{EC} $ and $m\angle {EAC} = 40^{\circ}.$ What is the measure of $\angle{B}?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that $\triangle{ABC}$ is an isosceles triangle with base $\overline{AB}.$ Consequently, the base angles must have equal measure:

\[ m\angle{BAC}=m\angle{B} \]

Also, since $\triangle{CEA}$ is an isosceles triangle, we have:

\[ m\angle{ C}=m\angle{EAC}=40^\circ \]

Finally, we calculate $m\angle {B}$ using the fact that the interior angles of $\triangle{ABC}$ sum to $180^\circ\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} m \angle {BAC} + m \angle {B} + m \angle {C} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] m \angle {B} + m \angle {B} + 40^\circ&= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 2m\angle {B} &= 140^\circ \\[3pt] m \angle {B} &= 70^\circ \end{align*}

question.text: Find the value of $z$ in the triangle shown above.
question.explanation:
First, from the diagram, notice that $\angle{CAB}$ and $\angle{BAD}$ are supplementary. Therefore, \begin{align*} m\angle{CAB} + m\angle{BAD} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle{CAB}+ z &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle{CAB} &= 180^\circ - z. \end{align*}

Since $\triangle{ABC}$ is an isosceles triangle where $\overline{AB} \cong \overline{BC}$, the base angles must be equal:

\[ m\angle{C} = m\angle{CAB}. \]

Finally, since the interior angles of any triangle sum to $180^\circ,$ we have \begin{align*} m\angle{CAB} + m\angle{C} + m\angle{B} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 2m\angle{CAB} + m\angle{B} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 2(180^\circ - z)+40^\circ &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 360^\circ - 2z+40^\circ &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 2z &= 220^\circ\\[3pt] z &= 110^\circ. \end{align*}
